question.text: What is the key difference between saving and investing?

answer.text: Saving focuses on safety and keeping money secure, while investing aims to grow money over time
Saving always gives higher returns than investing
Investing is only for young people, saving is for retired people
There is no difference — both terms mean the same thing

explanation.text: The Logic: Per the workbook, saving is linked to safety and the reduction of current consumption, and saving precedes investing. Investing, in turn, is undertaken to earn profits and is subject to a risk-return trade-off. The Trap: Saving does not "always" give higher returns, and investing is not restricted to any age group — both statements misrepresent the saving-versus-investing distinction. Note: The workbook frames the distinction in terms of purpose (safety/precaution vs. profit with risk-return trade-off), not in terms of guaranteed return comparisons between FDs and mutual funds.
